mechanism: Neutrophil extracellular traps (cell-free DNA, MPO-DNA, citrullinated histone H3)
human_direction: higher in severe or fatal disease: cfDNA rises from uncomplicated to cerebral malaria and separates fatal retinopathy-positive cases; NET counts, elastase and CitH3 rise with severity in falciparum and knowlesi malaria; sepsis meta-analyses report higher cfDNA in non-survivors. Counterpoint: in HU008 (341 ICU patients) cfDNA and MPO-DNA did not predict death after severity adjustment; only an ex vivo NET-induction assay did.

notes: Canine cfDNA fluorometry is linear and repeatable and is prognostic in canine sepsis (cfDNA per neutrophil higher in non-survivors, https://doi.org/10.1111/vec.12773); nucleosome ELISA (Nu.Q H3.1) and a histone-DNA ELISA have been evaluated in dogs. A dog cfDNA sequencing study (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ygeno.2018.05.020) detected Babesia DNA, not host NETs.

notes: Serum histones have been measured in dogs by ELISA in heatstroke (associated with severity) and in acute pancreatitis, and nucleosome assays in canine cancer, so a canine method exists. mechanism: Calprotectin (S100A8/A9) and S100A12 as circulating neutrophil activation alarmins
human_direction: higher with severity: a 21-cohort meta-analysis gives a pooled prognostic AUC of about 0.74 for circulating calprotectin in acute infection and sepsis; single cohorts link it to hospital mortality independently of renal function and to sepsis-associated AKI; S100A8/A9 genes sit in the neutrophil granule signature of severe malaria. Effects are moderate and calprotectin did not beat clinical severity scores.
